stories.headline: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning
stories.script: Our lead story today. The UK government says it is working to identify any potential exposure in its online services, after critical cyber-security flaws were identified in the PHP programming language that underpins a significant number of the world's websites. Governments and some of the world's biggest companies are rushing to protect systems that use PHP before hackers can exploit the flaws. The flaws were first discovered by AI, after which governments urged anyone who uses PHP to address them. A UK government spokesperson urged "all organisations, private and public, large and small" to follow guidance to protect their systems.

stories.headline: AI firms say UK has a year to head off datacentre protests before construction is threatened
stories.script: Turning to the United States. Exclusive: Nvidia, Microsoft and Cisco taskforce urges ministers to offer areas greater benefits from tech infrastructure amid fears of US-style opposition AI companies have told ministers they have 12 months to head off public opposition to datacentres in the UK or risk US-style protests that could threaten their construction. Successive dry summers and rising energy bills are increasing public scrutiny of plans for the huge computer warehouses that are used to train and run AI models, says a submission to the Labour government from a group including the AI infrastructure companies Nvidia, Microsoft and Cisco.

stories.headline: 1Password lets AI agents use your passwords without seeing them
stories.script: In other news. 1Password is introducing a new feature that allows AI agents to sign into your accounts without actually seeing or handling your passwords. The aptly named 1Password for Agents doesn't give bots free reign to access all of your connected accounts - you'll still need to grant approval for sign-in requests - but should make it less cumbersome to use Agents for tasks that require them to log into various services. stories.headline: Malaysia’s TuJu app struggles after Anwar suggests switching from Waze
stories.script: In Asia. Malaysia’s highway authority is working to resolve technical disruptions affecting its TuJu navigation application following a sharp increase in users. In a statement on Thursday, the Lembaga Lebuhraya Malaysia (LLM) said the matter was being resolved together with the application provider Prosignal Consortium. LLM said the surge in users came after Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim suggested that the public consider using a locally developed navigation application instead of Waze.

stories.headline: StreamEval: Evaluating Interactive Streaming Video Generation Models
stories.script: Around the world. As streaming video generation advances, enabling real-time interaction with generated video is becoming increasingly important. The researchers introduce StreamEval, a unified benchmark for interactive streaming video generation spanning five tasks: avatar dialogue, avatar performance, world generation, instruction editing, and reference editing. StreamEval comprises 300 scripted test cases lasting 15-300s, each specifying initial assets, incrementally arriving multimodal requests, and explicit requirements for state changes and content preservation. Performance is assessed along four evaluation dimensions: task execution, state consistency, visual fidelity, and audiovisual coordination, instantiated through ten task-specific metrics on a 0-100 scale. Evaluating 37 distinct models across 300 test cases, the researchers find that high visual quality and identity retention do not necessarily coincide with reliable request execution or sustained state consistency.
stories.whyThisMatters: As streaming video generation advances, enabling real-time interaction with generated video is becoming increasingly important.
keyPoints: StreamEval: Evaluating Interactive Streaming Video Generation Models

stories.headline: Meta beats expectations but legal penalties hit profit amid AI race
stories.script: Turning to the United States. Meta beat investor expectations for third-quarter revenue on Wednesday as it doubles down on a global AI race but the social media giant's profits took a hit due to an 18 billion dollars legal settlement with nearly all US states. The company reported 9.86 billion dollars in profits from July to September, almost 50 percent below investor expectations, which Meta said was dragged down by a 9.9 billion dollars charge related to the settlement.
